records.summary: A self-serve checker and deployment adapter for teams running Heroku-22 apps. It would check compatibility and help move build, configuration, and deployment workflows to Render, Railway, Fly.io, or self-hosting.

competitors.name: Heroku stack upgrade path
competitors.note: Heroku documents upgrading to a newer Heroku stack.

competitors.name: Render migration guide and MIT-licensed migration skill
competitors.note: Provides a migration workflow for moving from Heroku to Render.

rounds.plain: Render provides a migration guide and free migration skill for its platform, covering the core workflow for that destination.

risks: User base, paid customer count, and pricing are unverified.
The proposed adapter may duplicate Heroku's own migration tooling.
records.moat: The proposed maintained compatibility and dependency rules engine could accumulate edge-case mappings, but Render already provides a migration guide and free skill for one destination. No established mapping asset is evidenced.

records.summary: A self-serve inventory and compatibility report for custom and third-party Atlassian Connect apps. It would help Jira and Confluence administrators or app vendors assess migration to Forge or REST and webhook alternatives.
records.customer: Jira and Confluence administrators or app vendors

competitors.name: Atlassian adoption-status CLI and Forge migration tooling
competitors.note: Official Connect-to-Forge migration tools; pricing is unverified.

rounds.plain: Three official Connect-to-Forge migration releases landed within six months: an adoption-status CLI, macro mapping support, and a Confluence macro index feature. K2 means two or more competing launches in six months.

risks: User base, customer count, and pricing are unverified.
Atlassian's Cloud Migration Assistants support app data migration.
records.moat: The proposed compatibility catalogue and migration test fixtures could accumulate mappings, but no established asset is evidenced. Atlassian has released migration tools and messaging.

records.summary: A self-serve audit, export, and conversion tool for MSPs moving VSA 9 configurations to independent RMM alternatives such as NinjaOne or N-able. Kaseya says VSA 9 will be decommissioned on 2027-08-31 and directs customers to Datto RMM or VSA 10.

revenue_claims.claim: Kaseya reported more than 40,000 MSP and SMB customers globally in 2026; this is its overall customer base, not VSA 9 users.

competitors.name: Kaseya migration routes to Datto RMM or VSA 10
ProVal VSA 9-to-Datto migration solution
competitors.note: Published 2026-10-16; supports migration to Datto, not cross-vendor policy or script conversion.

competitors.name: NinjaOne
competitors.price: $1.50 per endpoint/month at 10,000 endpoints to $3.75 at 50 or fewer
competitors.note: Published pricing range; regional and product variation applies.

rounds.plain: The mapping library is prospective rather than evidenced. K0 means the moat is too weak to take three or more months to copy.
No official or partner tool mapping VSA 9 configurations to independent RMMs was found; one Datto-specific migration solution was found.

risks: VSA 9 user count, active installs, independent switcher count, demand, and payment evidence are unverified.
A self-serve write-back converter may be difficult because target API and import capabilities differ.
Migration requires handling credentials and customer configurations securely.
A mature service's owner hours and automation share are estimates, not demonstrated.
records.moat: A versioned, field-tested mapping library could become a data asset, but no compiled dataset or validated conversion behavior is evidenced. The migration appears deadline-driven and one-time, with weak switching costs and network effects.

hours.note: A mature audit-and-export service could plausibly fit within this time if onboarding, billing, reporting, and routine support are automated; this is an operating hypothesis.

records.next_steps: Before building, check exact-match search volume and bid ranges for VSA 9 migration and VSA-to-NinjaOne/N-able migration in the US, UK, and relevant European markets. Record location and date settings; treat this as a demand screen, not proof of willingness to pay.

records.summary: A self-serve workflow inventory, archive, and conversion package for publishers and content teams using WoodWing Smart Mover. Support ended 2026-03-27, the stated EOL is 2027-03-27, and existing customers can continue under a transition support plan through 2029-03-31.
records.customer: Publishers and content teams using Smart Mover

revenue_claims.claim: WoodWing reports 1,500+ customers and 100,000+ users across its products; Smart Mover usage is not specified.

competitors.name: WoodWing Transition Support Plan
competitors.note: Continues existing agreements at the customer's existing, unpublished rate and includes advice on moving workflows.

competitors.name: Enfocus Switch Core Engine plus Metadata
Impressed alternatives/migration article
competitors.note: Published 2026-06-04; provides alternatives and migration guidance.

competitors.name: 3f8h.net migration work
competitors.note: Advertises migration work across n8n, Enfocus Switch, and WoodWing Connect; launch date unverified.

rounds.plain: The proposed moat is not established, and estimated automation share is 45%. K0 means the moat is too weak to take three or more months to copy; K1 means it breaks a hard rule.

A version-specific parser and validated mappings are plausible assets, while WoodWing's transition plan offers advice rather than a self-serve archive or converter. Customer count, pricing, and payment evidence remain unverified.

risks: Smart Mover customer count, active deployments, pricing, and payment evidence are unverified.
The 2027 EOL is not a universal shutdown date: transition support can continue through 2029-03-31.
WoodWing offers migration advice and fee credit toward its own replacement project.
Estimated automation share is 45%, and owner hours are unverified.
Reliable conversion appears customer-specific and service-heavy.
records.moat: A parser and permissioned library of validated mappings could become a data asset, but neither currently exists. Public task documentation and migration consultancies make a basic parser easier to copy; there is no demonstrated network effect or recurring switching cost.

hours.note: Unverified; bespoke mapping and customer validation could exceed this.

records.next_steps: Test a read-only workflow inventory report using a sample based on public documentation. Seek qualified opt-ins, real anonymized exports, and paid-pilot requests; ask whether the report solves an inventory problem before investing in conversion.

The opportunity depends on customers choosing alternatives outside Apliqo.
